section_summary: This section contains policy decisions, draft directives, and transmittal correspondence from the Far Eastern Commission and State-War-Navy Coordinating Committee concerning the comprehensive revision of the post-war Japanese educational system, emphasizing democratization, the elimination of militarism and State Shinto, and administrative decentralization. It also includes departmental inquiries and correspondence regarding occupation educational policies and school conditions, notably from scholar Robert King Hall and SCAP education officer Helen Heffernan. Finally, it features a detailed GHQ SCAP publications analysis surveying contemporary articles by Japanese educators on curriculum reform, teacher training, scientific thinking, and modern pedagogical techniques.

subfiles.about: Enclosure setting forth Far Eastern Commission policy and guiding principles for reforming the Japanese educational system.
subfiles.summary: Draft directive detailing Far Eastern Commission policy to democratize Japanese education, including teacher screening and training, curriculum and textbook revision, elimination of militarism and State Shinto, decentralization, and expanding compulsory schooling.
subfiles.title: Policy for the Revision of the Japanese Educational System (FEC-092/1)
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers

subfiles.about: Certified excerpts from the minutes of the Far Eastern Commission's 51st meeting regarding the policy for revising the Japanese educational system.
subfiles.summary: Certified minutes recording Indian and Australian statements on educational policy FEC-092/1, debating employment restrictions on purged teachers, State Shinto versus state religion, and the timing and extent of educational decentralization under SCAP.
subfiles.title: Certified Excerpts from the Minutes of the Fifty-First Meeting of the Far Eastern Commission

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum transmitting to SWNCC a draft directive and minutes excerpts on Japanese educational reform for forwarding to General MacArthur.
subfiles.summary: Assistant Secretary of State Hilldring requests that SWNCC forward an enclosed draft directive to the Joint Chiefs of Staff for transmission to General MacArthur, implementing the Far Eastern Commission's March 27, 1947 policy decision. The enclosures include the full draft directive on democratizing Japanese education, purging militarist teachers, eliminating Shinto indoctrination, and reforming curricula, along with minutes containing Indian and Australian statements on teacher disqualifications, state religion, and administrative decentralization.
subfiles.title: Draft Directive Regarding Policy for the Revision of the Japanese Educational System

subfiles.about: Certified duplicate copy of the State Department memorandum and enclosures transmitting the Japanese educational reform directive to SWNCC.
subfiles.summary: A duplicate record copy of Assistant Secretary Hilldring's April 2, 1947 memorandum to SWNCC, with accompanying enclosures. It transmits the draft directive implementing the Far Eastern Commission's policy on Japanese educational reform to General MacArthur via the Joint Chiefs of Staff, accompanied by excerpts of meeting minutes detailing Indian and Australian reservations.
subfiles.title: Draft Directive Regarding Policy for the Revision of the Japanese Educational System (Copy)

subfiles.about: SWNCC memorandum transmitting three copies of Directive Serial No. 74 sent to General MacArthur regarding Japanese educational reform.
subfiles.summary: SWNCC Secretary Moseley transmits copies of Directive Serial No. 74, sent on April 5, 1947 by the Joint Chiefs of Staff to General MacArthur, to the Secretary of State for transmittal to the Far Eastern Commission and departmental files. The enclosed directive outlines policies for Japanese educational reform, mandating democratic principles, screening of militaristic teachers, prohibition of military training and State Shinto, textbook revision, and eventual administrative decentralization.
subfiles.title: Directive Transmitted to SCAP by the Joint Chiefs of Staff (Serial No. 74)

subfiles.about: Memorandum transmitting a certified copy of Directive Serial No. 74 to the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.summary: Memorandum enclosing a certified copy of Directive Serial No. 74 to SCAP for filing with the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.title: Directive Serial No. 74 to SCAP Regarding Revision of the Japanese Educational System

subfiles.about: Letter requesting official copies of occupation educational directives and constitution drafts for an academic study on post-war Japan.
subfiles.summary: Robert King Hall of Columbia University requests copies of educational directives and the new Japanese Constitution for a forthcoming book, while critiquing errors and editorial deficiencies in a State Department publication on Japanese occupation policy.
subfiles.title: Inquiry Regarding Japanese Educational Documents
subfiles.to: Director, Office of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: Department of State reference slip routing Robert King Hall's inquiry on educational occupation policy.
subfiles.summary: Department of State Form DS-10 reference slip routing Robert King Hall's letter concerning occupation education policies.
subfiles.title: Reference Slip Regarding Robert King Hall Letter

subfiles.about: Department of State file routing sheet stamped by the Division of Northeast Asian Affairs.
subfiles.summary: Division of Northeast Asian Affairs date stamp and filing routing slip dated July 21, 1947.
subfiles.title: Division of Northeast Asian Affairs File Sheet

subfiles.about: Letter discussing an atomic energy peace essay, Japan's new constitution, and severe material shortages in Japanese schools.
subfiles.summary: Helen Heffernan discusses Lady Butterfield's peace essay, Japan's new pacifist constitution, and critical shortages of teachers and school supplies.
subfiles.title: Letter Regarding Atomic Energy Essay and Japanese Educational Conditions

subfiles.about: Despatch forwarding a GHQ SCAP report analyzing Japanese articles and professional opinions on teaching methods and educational reform.
subfiles.summary: The Counselor of Mission forwards a GHQ SCAP Civil Information and Education Section analysis of Japanese educational publications. The report examines Japanese educators' enthusiasm for democratic schooling, covering the fostering of student independence, discussion techniques, scientific inquiry, technical and arts education, and debates over history and textbook revisions. It highlights contributions from prominent scholars and teachers across Japan grappling with post-war educational reconstruction.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1316: Transmittal of a Report Concerning Teachers and Teaching Methods
